post_result_plateau_diagnostic.interpretation: additional positives often eliminated candidate source/barrier/analyst worlds without enlarging the set of nodes unreachable in every surviving undirected world

interpretation: Reachability-aware positive occurrences carried substantial information that local A/B viability alone could not provide.
Spatially dispersed anchors were more discriminating than clustered anchors at equal counts in the preregistered 25 percent and 50 percent contrasts.
Complete positive occurrence coverage still left severe world and source ambiguity.
The predeclared expectation that more positive anchors would recover progressively more robust impossibility was refuted: robust-impossibility recovery plateaued immediately in every eligible row.

The v4 refutation points to a structural limitation of static undirected connectivity worlds: more occurrence anchors can reduce world identity without necessarily changing the union of reachable components.
The next valid virtual-world question is whether directed movement and temporal flow break this plateau and make occurrence order informative about source and impossibility.
claim_boundary: The candidate-source universe is synthetic and the source counts are not ancestry probabilities.
The dispersed-anchor advantage is an information result under equal synthetic point counts, not a field sampling recommendation.
The O5 plateau is specific to this frozen static undirected candidate-world family and is not asserted as universal.
